objective: Prefer substantial reference-style improvement while permitting explicitly described minor semantic drift; retain warnings instead of a binary NLI veto.

drift_rubric.none_detected: No substantive change identified by the assessor; not proof of equivalence.
drift_rubric.minor: Limited loss of detail, emphasis or nuance with the main propositions, actors, quantities and direction intact.
drift_rubric.moderate: A supporting proposition, qualification or scope changes materially, while the central conclusion remains recognizable.
drift_rubric.high: A central proposition, actor/role, quantity, causal direction, essential condition or conclusion changes.
drift_rubric.unknown: Evidence is insufficient to assign severity. Never relabel low entailment or abstention as minor drift.

style_rubric.none: No identifiable movement toward the paired author's reference style.
style_rubric.slight: Small movement toward reference rhetoric/expression, or mostly generic formalization.
style_rubric.moderate: Several concrete reference-style features improve without being explained solely by a longer sentence.
style_rubric.large: Clear, sustained reference-grounded transformation across paragraph, sentence and language features.

limitations: Weights and qualitative rubrics are exploratory policy choices, not validated severity probabilities or an authorship classifier. Original frozen experiment scores are unchanged.
